subject: Genetics
title: The Genome's Promise
description: A fast breakdown of The Genome's Promise for builders.

hook.text: The Human Genome Project promised a medical revolution. Twenty years later, that revolution is finally arriving.

buildup.text: Gene therapies now cure blindness and sickle cell disease. mRNA vaccines—built on genomic knowledge—fought COVID.

discovery.text: Precision oncology matches cancer treatment to tumor genetics. Survival rates for some cancers doubled in a decade.

twist.text: The revolution was slower than promised. It took 20 years of infrastructure, data, and tools before payoffs arrived.

climax.text: The genome project was an investment in foundations. The returns are compounding now—and will for generations.

punchline.text: The promise was 20 years early. It wasn't wrong.

quiz.question: How did the genome project contribute to COVID response?
options: Genomic knowledge enabled mRNA vaccine development
